articles.title: Home Assistant Cloud prepares to become Home Assistant Link
articles.dek: Nabu Casa plans the new name for December 2; the existing subscription needs no action from its users.
body: Nabu Casa plans to rename Home Assistant Cloud to Home Assistant Link on December 2. The company says the subscription stays the same and existing subscribers do not need to do anything.

Carl Albertsson explains that the old name led some people to think Home Assistant runs in the cloud. It continues to run locally at home; the optional subscription connects services such as remote access, voice assistants and online backups. Ending that subscription does not stop the underlying smart home working.
Nabu Casa says the majority of subscription profits fund the Open Home Foundation. The announcement invites community feedback before the intended change in Home Assistant’s December 2026.12 release.

articles.title: Home Assistant restores local app sources to full backups
articles.dek: A renamed folder had caused full backups to skip the source files for locally developed apps.
body: Home Assistant corrects a backup omission affecting people who keep locally developed apps on their system. Full backups had silently skipped the local app source folder after its on-disk location changed from addons to apps.

Mike Degatano makes backup and restore operations find the new location while keeping the old folder name inside the backup format. Existing backups and clients retain that compatibility; the correction does not recover files absent from an earlier backup.

pullRequests.title: Fix full backups not including local apps folder

articles.title: ESPHome sends smaller firmware updates over wireless links
articles.dek: Compression cuts transfer sizes on ESP32 and Pico devices, with larger time savings on an unreliable connection.
body: ESPHome compresses wireless firmware updates on ESP32, RP2040 and LibreTiny devices, extending an option previously used on ESP8266. In J. Nick Koston’s board tests, the ESP32 transfer shrank from 762 KB to 534 KB and the Pico W transfer from 515 KB to 353 KB.

On the Pico W, three transfers took about 6.3–6.5 seconds instead of 9.3–9.6 seconds, with roughly 1.5 seconds added to the restart while the device unpacked the image. In an encrypted ESP32 test with 15% simulated packet loss, the two compressed transfers took 67 and 74 seconds, compared with 113 and 317 seconds without compression.
The uploader and device negotiate compression, keeping older firmware and command-line tools compatible. A device without enough spare memory accepts an ordinary upload.

pullRequests.title: [esphome][ota][core] Compress OTA uploads on ESP32, RP2040, LibreTiny and host

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps counting failed logins after a bad hostname
articles.dek: An unreadable network lookup no longer disables the failed-login counter and its log entry.
body: Home Assistant keeps recording failed sign-ins when the connecting address has an unreadable reverse-DNS hostname. That lookup is only needed to add a name to the log, but an invalid response could interrupt processing before the failure was counted.

Guillaume BAILLEUL prevents that lookup error from bypassing the failed-login counter used for IP banning. It also preserves the normal unauthorized response instead of returning a server error. This is his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Fix 500 instead of 401 when reverse DNS lookup fails to decode

articles.title: ESPHome carries serial equipment across the local network
articles.dek: Makers can connect serial equipment to a remote ESPHome device without a direct cable between them.
body: ESPHome gives makers a network path to serial equipment. One component carries a device’s physical serial port over a TCP network connection; another presents that network stream as a serial port that existing ESPHome components can use. Both copy the data unchanged in each direction.

Bascht74 supplies client and server modes, with each listening bridge accepting one connected peer. An optional list limits connections to specified IPv4 addresses or networks; leaving it out accepts any address. The connection carries raw data without encryption or password authentication. J. Nick Koston reviewed the implementation and its companion guides.

articles.title: Music Assistant finds Bandcamp purchases missing from the library
articles.dek: Single-track purchases and albums bought with physical releases join the collection, while failed lookups stop wiping saved items.
body: Music Assistant fills gaps in Bandcamp libraries by including individually purchased tracks and albums bought with vinyl, cassette or CD packages. Alexey ALERT Rubashёff also keeps hidden and preorder tracks visible as unavailable instead of losing them from the album.

A failed album or artist lookup no longer ends the entire library synchronization. An incomplete paginated response fails safely instead of treating the missing entries as removals and clearing their favourites. A Bandcamp outage during startup also stops leaving the source unloaded until Music Assistant restarts.

Collection pages use the information already returned in their listings instead of requesting each entry separately. In the contributor’s test, a 124-entry public collection opened in 6.8 seconds rather than 39 and included 12 previously missing package albums. David Bishop reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: Make the Bandcamp provider more reliable and complete its library

articles.title: Shelly radiator valves need a gateway with explicit BLU TRV support
articles.dek: Corrected guidance replaces the broader generation-and-firmware rule reported on September 27.
body: Check for built-in BLU TRV support when choosing a Shelly gateway for its radiator valves. Home Assistant’s corrected guidance names the Shelly BLU Gateway Gen3 or other Shelly devices with that explicit support; generation 2 or newer hardware and firmware 2.1.0 alone are not enough.
The September 27 edition reported the earlier, broader compatibility guidance. Maciej Bieniek corrects it after a misunderstanding with the Shelly team, ahead of Home Assistant’s October release.

pullRequests.title: Update the information about the Shelly BLU TRV

articles.title: ENGIE Belgium energy prices join Home Assistant
articles.dek: The new connection supplies gas and electricity prices per kilowatt-hour.
body: Home Assistant adds an ENGIE Belgium connection for households following their gas and electricity prices. Its first set of readings covers the price per kilowatt-hour for each energy type.

Daan Vervacke brings the connection into Home Assistant after developing a community integration with help from other Belgian testers. Purpose-specific triggers and conditions from that earlier integration are not part of this initial addition.

pullRequests.title: Add ENGIE Belgium integration

articles.title: Home Assistant turns Mealie shopping text into ingredients
articles.dek: Quantities, units and ingredient names can be separated automatically, with a plain-note fallback.
body: Adding “1 kg Chicken” to a Mealie shopping list through Home Assistant can create a structured ingredient rather than a single text note. The integration asks Mealie’s parser to separate the quantity, unit and ingredient, falling back to a note when confidence is low.

Andrew Jackson adds a choice of parser and separate controls for parsing added and edited items. Keeping those switches separate lets a person correct a bad interpretation without forcing the edit through the parser again.

pullRequests.title: Add Mealie parser to to-do lists

articles.title: Matter.js closes pairing windows that stayed open indefinitely
articles.dek: A rejected overlapping request also stops leaving further pairing attempts stuck until a restart.
body: Devices built with Matter.js close pairing windows they open themselves, correcting a timer that was created but never started. The default window lasts 48 hours on an unpaired device and 15 minutes on one already paired; explicitly opening it again restarts the timer.

Ingo Fischer also prevents a failed request from leaving the device permanently answering Busy until it restarts. An administrator’s request can replace a window the device opened itself, while a window opened by another administrator still blocks an overlapping request.

pullRequests.title: fix(node): close a node's own commissioning window, and let an administrator's window replace it

articles.title: Home Assistant sends destinations to Tesla navigation
articles.dek: Automations can send an address, map link or coordinates to the car.
body: Tesla Fleet gains Home Assistant actions for sending a navigation destination to a vehicle. One accepts an address, place name or map link; the other accepts latitude and longitude. Both wake the car first and require permission to issue vehicle commands.
Matti Hiljanen tested both forms on a 2024 Model 3 Highland, which received the address and coordinates. This is his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Add navigation actions to Tesla Fleet

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps cancelled CalDAV events out of schedules
articles.dek: Called-off appointments no longer appear as active calendar events, including one cancelled occurrence in a series.
body: Home Assistant excludes cancelled CalDAV events from both its event list and the search for the current or next appointment. A calendar such as Nextcloud can retain a cancelled entry instead of deleting it; Home Assistant had continued to treat that entry as going ahead.

Tom Mittelstädt also handles a cancelled occurrence within a repeating series without removing the other dates. The calendar-status work reported on September 2 had left this filtering for a later step.

pullRequests.title: Filter cancelled events out of caldav

articles.title: Home Assistant’s iPhone app stops waiting on a stalled watch
articles.dek: A slow watch synchronization no longer prevents the dashboard’s first page from loading.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app keeps opening its dashboard when synchronization with Apple Watch stalls. Several simultaneous watch updates at launch could previously occupy every available worker and leave the first page unloaded.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves processes watch updates separately and combines repeated requests, so a stalled watch connection cannot occupy the workers needed to open the dashboard. Manually requested synchronization and watch-face reloads also gain a timeout.

pullRequests.title: Run the watch context sync off the cooperative pool on iOS
